title: Cohort SLI orchestration and trace anchors notebook
body:
Purpose:
This note collects an approach for stitching cohort-level SLIs (customer cohorts, model-version cohorts, and routing-policy cohorts) with lightweight trace anchors so operators can get rapid, cost-bounded investigations for regression signals.

Context & motivation:
- We frequently see noisy global SLIs that hide cohort regressions (example: burst of slow token tail for a handful of dedicated tenants).
- Full-trace capture for all requests is expensive (trace storage + query costs). We want high-fidelity anchors for suspicious cohorts with cheap probe panels and targeted trace sampling.
- Goal: enable 2–3 minute mean-time-to-hypothesis for oncall before full-blown rollout rollback.

High-level strategy:
1) Cohort-first SLI layer: compute SLIs partitioned by cohort keys (tenant_id, model_alias, rollout_tag). Aggregate in two horizons: 1m streaming (probe) and 5m rolling (SLO).
2) Lightweight trace anchors: store compact span index metadata for 1% baseline + up to 10% for cohorts under investigation (adaptive). Anchors include: trace_id, top-3 span names, latency buckets, kv_cache_hit, prompt_len, model_version.
3) Probe panels on dashboards: cheap aggregations and anomaly detection feed into an escalation automation that increases trace sampling for the affected cohort.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical names):
- sli.request_p99_per_cohort (type: distribution-derived quantile)
  - cohort_keys: [tenant_id, model_alias, rollout_tag]
  - aggregation: p99 over 5m window, per-cohort; derived from token-level latency timestamps.
  - alert threshold: bursty deviation > 2x baseline p99 for 5m
  - owner: eng-observability

- sli.kvcache_hit_rate_cohort (type: ratio)
  - numerator: requests with kv_cache_hit=true in window
  - denominator: requests total in window
  - aggregation: 1m and 1h windows
  - use: detect prefix/cold-start regressions leading to latency spikes
  - owner: serving-runtime

- sli.cpu_token_time_per_model (type: rate)
  - units: ms-token per second aggregated by model_alias
  - purpose: spot inefficient kernels/quantization regressions
  - owner: infra/serving

- probe.synthetic_sli_cohort_fastfail (type: synthetic)
  - short test prompt (deterministic) routed to cohort; measure ttf (time-to-first-token) and first-200-token p50
  - cadence: 30s per cohort sample (rotating)
  - owner: obs-synthetic-team

Trace anchor design (compact index):
- anchor fields (kept as high-cardinality-safe strings): trace_id, cohort_id, request_ts, top_span, total_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, model_version, routing_path, token_count, sample_reason
- retention tiers: 7d full anchor index; 30d aggregated metrics derived from anchors; raw spans kept only for sampled traces and debug window (configurable per-customer for private deployments)
- sampling policy:
  - baseline: uniform 1% global traces for telemetry and model quality checks
  - cohort elevation: when cohort probe SLI crosses threshold, escalate cohort to 10% for 10m, 25% for 5m if escalation continues
  - emergency: if error-rate > X% or p99 > Y ms, capture full trace for 100% of a small token-sampled subset (e.g., first 50 requests after trigger)

Minimal span attribute spec (trace payload cost control):
- mandatory attributes: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, start_ns, duration_ns, span_name, cohort_id, model_version, kv_cacheHit (boolean), call_type (inference|embed|rerank), prompt_hash
- optional attributes (only for elevated sampling): full_prompt, response_excerpt, gpu_id, kernel_version

Dashboard panel design notes (cost-aware):
- Top row (cheap probes): cohort SLI sparkline (1m streaming), kv_cache_hit_rate, synthetic_probe_latency. Panels use pre-aggregated rollups (no raw trace lookups).
- Middle row (investigation): cohort-weighted heatmap of p50/p95/p99 across model_alias x tenant shading; clickable drilldown opens filtered trace index query (trace anchors).
- Drill flow: panel -> query builder pre-filled -> anchor results (compact) -> option to pull raw spans for selected trace_ids.
- Panel tiling: assign each panel a "query-cost budget" (e.g., 10 QPS across dashboards) and use cached results for 30s to avoid query storms during incidents.

Investigation runway example (operator playbook):
1) Alert fires on sli.request_p99_per_cohort for tenant T (p99 2.5x baseline).
2) Ops dashboard shows anchor hits: kv_cache_hit_rate dropped to 18% (baseline 87%). Probe synthetic also slow.
3) Elevate sampling for tenant T automatically (10% for 10m). Anchor list returns 3 traces with top_span model.infer.attention.
4) Operator requests raw spans for trace_id X -> observes large kernel fallback path and increased memcpy times.
5) Rollback model rollout_tag R if correlated, otherwise increase cache warming and throttle bursts.

Query snippets (for runbook):
- fast cohort p99: SELECT cohort_id, quantile(0.99)(latency_ms) FROM request_latency WHERE cohort_id = 'T' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY cohort_id
- kv cache rate: SELECT cohort_id, sum(kv_cache_hit)::float / count(*) FROM request_events WHERE ts > now()- '1 minute' GROUP BY cohort_id
- anchor lookup: SELECT trace_id, top_span, total_latency_ms FROM trace_anchors WHERE cohort_id = 'T' AND ts > now()- '15 minutes' ORDER BY total_latency_ms DESC LIMIT 50

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we index rollout_tag as part of cohort_id by default? (tradeoff: higher cardinality)
- Sampling escalation knobs: sensible default percentages for low-traffic cohorts vs high-traffic cohorts. Proposal: floor 1% / escalate to 10% / 25% / emergency 100% of small sample.
- How do we bill trace storage for private deployments? Include per-customer retention config in UI?

Planned short-term actions (next 4 weeks):
- [Ava] create Confluence spec for anchor format + retention (due 2026-03-17)
- [Liam] prototype dashboard tiles with query-cost budget gating (POC by 2026-03-24)
- [Priya] add cohort keys to streaming SLI pipeline (schema + consumers, PR: #214)
- [Diego] implement sampling escalation API (backend hook, MVP 2026-04-07)

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Consider a "cohort-hint" header that clients can set for known long-tail experiments to avoid misattribution.
- Add a small ML detector (rolling median + MAD) to flag kv_cache sudden shifts rather than absolute thresholds.

References and links:
- Confluence draft: confluence://obs/docs/COHORT-SLI-ORCH (linked_artifacts)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-329 (incident automation for sampling escalation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/214 (streaming SLI cohort keys)

If you read nothing else: prioritize getting kv_cache_hit_rate into the 1m probe row and wire an automated sampling escalation so operators can see anchors immediately when a cohort shows degradation.

Last updated: 2026-03-10 by Ava Martinez
